name: Satisfactory
notes: Launch args: -NO_EOS_OVERLAY -dx11 -USEALLAVAILABLECORES -Nosplash -ResX=1280 -ResY=720 (Steam LaunchOptions; was wrongly matched to -NOTEXTURESTREAMING earlier). D3DMetal 3.0. Crash-avoidance (not taste): MetalFX=0, D3DM_ENABLE_ASYNC_COMMIT=0, HUD off. MetalFX on crawls ~0.1–2 fps then RHIThread SIGILL in D3DMCommandQueue::ExecuteCommandLists; MetalFX off alone also SIGILL'd. wyn play waits 120s after quit (D3DMetal GPU settle). Leftover CrashReportClient does not block Play once the game EXE is gone. avxEnabled stays true — next knob if this trio still SIGILLs. TWO OTHER FAILURES, both measured 12 Sep 2026, neither the ExecuteCommandLists SIGILL above — do not conflate the three. (1) DEATH IN THE MENU AT ~33s, no LogExit, no UE crash handler, no macOS crash report, and the log's last line is the crawl in its own words: TicksCount=[421] ExpectedTicksCount=[1000]. Cause was not this profile: wyn play reused a Steam client that was already running, and a game inherits the client's environment and nothing else, so it got gameHostSteamEnvironment's D3DM_ENABLE_METALFX=1 default over this profile's 0 — the MetalFX crawl-then-SIGILL, reached by the back door. Fixed by SteamLauncher+SessionEnv.swift (Phase 0 in launchGameViaSteam restarts a client whose recorded env disagrees). If this recurs, check that fix is in the wyn you are actually running, not just in the tree. (2) EXIT CRASH on the quit path: quitting from the in-game menu tears down in order — online services, Steam API unload, FFX/FSR/DLSS module shutdown, EOS_Shutdown EOS_Success — then the process dies with FMallocBinned2 Attempt to realloc an unrecognized block, canary == 0x0 != 0xe3 (MallocBinned2.cpp:900). Heap corruption on exit, not OOM. It costs nothing in play — that run was ~26 minutes with /Game/FactoryGame/Map/GameLevel01/Persistent_Level loaded and a person playing — but it means no LogExit: Exiting., so a §5 clean exit cannot be claimed from a menu quit, and no crash directory is written despite the fatal error. Undiagnosed. Do not read it as a launch failure.
